questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech. "I'll see you later," she said.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

"I'll see you later," she said.

options.text: She said that she would see me later.
options.html: She said that she would see me later.

options.text: She said that she will see you later.
options.html: She said that she will see you later.

options.text: She said that she would be seeing me later.
options.html: She said that she would be seeing me later.

options.text: She said that she will be able to see you later.
options.html: She said that she will be able to see you later.

questions.solution:
The sentence in the Direct Speech is in Future Simple Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Indirect Speech should be in Present Conditional Tense.

Future Simple (Subject + will/shall + V1 + object) should be converted into Present Conditional (Subject + would/should + V1 +object).

For example:

He said, "I will be in Kolkata on Friday." (Direct Speech)

He said that he would be in Kolkata on Friday. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

· 'Will' changes to 'would'.

· Subjective verb 'I' changes to 'she'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: (a).

options.html: Will you please do your work properly?

options.text: Can you please do your work properly?
options.html: Can you please do your work properly?

questions.solution:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive Voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The question in Active voice is in the imperative form. An imperative sentence is used to express order, request, suggestion, etc. They begin with a principal verb. Here, the imperative sentence in Active voice is a request.

In Active voice, the use of "please", "kindly" is present. In Passive voice, the use of "please" or "kindly" is removed. "You are requested" is added in the Passive voice.

The format in Active voice is: V1 + Object.

Thus, the format in Passive voice will be: You are requested to + V1 + Object.

For example:

Kindly, wash the dishes as soon as possible. (Active)

You are requested to wash the dishes as soon as possible. (Passive)

Please note that, "You are kindly requested to..." is a wrong usage.

Therefore, the correct answer is: (a).

questions.question: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. These kinds of sharks are known as obligate ram ventilators because they draw water in through their mouths and force it out through their gills. B. They use a method called buccal pumping, in which water is pulled in through the mouth and forced out through the gills by the cheek muscles. C. It is true that many types of sharks must keep moving in order to receive life-giving oxygen from the water passing through their gills. D. Other types of sharks are able to remain stationary because they possess special structures called spiracles, which force water out through their gills.
questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. These kinds of sharks are known as obligate ram ventilators because they draw water in through their mouths and force it out through their gills.

B. They use a method called buccal pumping, in which water is pulled in through the mouth and forced out through the gills by the cheek muscles.

C. It is true that many types of sharks must keep moving in order to receive life-giving oxygen from the water passing through their gills.

D. Other types of sharks are able to remain stationary because they possess special structures called spiracles, which force water out through their gills.
questions.solution:
'C' is the first sentence as it introduces the main subject 'types of sharks', it is followed by 'A' as it gives a name to the types of sharks mentioned in 'C'. How they breathe is mentioned in 'A' and what the whole process is called (i.e. buccal pumping), is mentioned in 'B'. 'D' is the final sentence as it talks about the other types of sharks that are stationary, so it is an independent sentence and can be used at the end of the paragraph. Therefore, the correct order of rearrangement is CABD.

Hence, option (a) is correct.

She hoped that the mice would no longer be afraid to come near her. C. questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. An old mouse, who was wise enough to keep his distance, whispered to a friend, "Many a bag have I seen in my day, but never one with a cat's head".

B. She hoped that the mice would no longer be afraid to come near her.

C. A cat, grown feeble with age and no longer able to hunt mice as she once did, thought to herself how she might entice them within reach of her paw.

D. Thinking that she might pass herself off for a bag or for a dead cat at least, she suspended herself by the hind legs from a peg.
questions.solution:
'C' is the introductory sentence as it introduces the 'cat' and what she thought, it is further expressed in 'D'. 'D' describes her condition that she seems like a dead cat, so what a mice will feel after looking at her is mentioned in 'B'. 'A' is an independent sentence as it describes what a mouse will think, so it can be placed at the end of the sentence. The correct rearrangement is CDBA.

Hence, option (d) is correct.
